summary: Task Management remains strategically well-shaped and governable, but downstream operational readiness is still constrained by the Vega/PXS boundary failure, an only-partially-executable PXS consumption contract, and unresolved proof/feedback gaps in the canonical operating substrate. TOP_PRIORITIES.md was reviewed against the current product stack and remains aligned with the strongest current bottlenecks, so no priority refresh change was required in this run.
top_priorities: Close the Vega/PXS boundary readiness gap and rerun it to PASS.
Deliver a minimal executable pxs consumption contract with schemas, explicit transport semantics, and worked examples.
Stabilize and prove the canonical substrate that pxs will consume, including explicit GO/NO-GO evidence on the DB-cutover proof path.

blockers.title: Vega/PXS boundary readiness remains a hard gate for safe downstream consumption
blockers.next_step: Close the failing boundary conditions and rerun the acceptance sheet to PASS with evidence.

blockers.title: Control Panel to TDE assignment path is not yet operationally trustworthy because insertion can occur without explicit acceptance or runner pickup
blockers.next_step: Treat assignment acceptance and visibility as required interface work: route assignments through canonical intake, return explicit acceptance states, and eliminate silent limbo.

risks.title: R-001 Vega/PXS boundary readiness failure blocks safe downstream consumption
risks.impact: Downstream Task Management consumption remains unsafe, ad hoc, or coupled across domains until the boundary acceptance conditions pass.
risks.mitigation: Keep boundary readiness as the top gating dependency and rerun acceptance to PASS with evidence.

risks.title: R-002 Readiness description can outrun readiness evidence
risks.impact: Consumers may build on a substrate whose readiness is described more strongly than it is currently proven.
risks.mitigation: Keep readiness claims tied to explicit GO/NO-GO evidence, decision records, and compact review surfaces.

risks.title: R-003 Downstream consumption remains softer than the internal product model suggests
risks.impact: Adoption in pxs stays bespoke and fragile if schemas, compatibility/versioning semantics, and examples remain under-specified.
risks.mitigation: Upgrade the consumption interface into a minimal executable contract with validation and worked examples.

risks.title: R-005 Shadow operating state / silent limbo path
risks.impact: Producers can mistake task insertion for operational acceptance, degrading trust in TDE as the execution system of record.
risks.mitigation: Use the assignment acceptance contract and canonical intake path so acceptance, no-runner, and binding failures are explicit.

proposed_tde_actions: Triage the Vega/PXS boundary PASS dependency as the top active signal for downstream consumption readiness.
Prioritize the minimal executable pxs consumption contract as the next interface-hardening step.
Create or update TDE work to close the Control Panel assignment acceptance / silent-limbo gap before treating producer-side pushes as reliable.
Maintain a visible readiness-evidence path for the canonical substrate, including explicit DB-cutover GO/NO-GO closure.
